text: Hey team, quick question—does anyone remember how Marketo behavior scoring works? Specifically, like, what triggers the points and how often someone can get scored?

Yeah, Tom, I can help. So behavior scoring is all about what actions the person takes—like attending events, downloading stuff, that kind of thing. Each action has a set number of points, and you can get scored every time you do the thing (like, every time you attend a conference or download content). But once the Person Score goes over 300, the behavior scoring gets nulled out. For campaigns, you only get points if there’s a 'success'—I think the details are on the programs page in the handbook, under progression statuses.

Oh, and for example, attending a webcast is +40 points, attending online stuff is +20, conference booth visits are +20, and content syndication downloads are +10. There’s a table somewhere in the handbook if you need the full list.
Super helpful, Sara, thanks! That clears it up for me too.
